summary: Unexpected egress path flips after pin healthcheck causing region latency variance
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent p95 latency spikes and region egress flips after our pin healthcheck runs. Impact: Notifyly experiences periodic p95 increases from ~120ms to ~450ms for requests that have a region pin to eu-west; spikes correlate with a router healthcheck window. Environment: Dedicated account on prod us-east control plane with residency pin set to eu-west for workspace 'notifyly-prod'. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send steady traffic pinned to eu-west from app clients in us-east. 2) Observe stable p95 ~120ms for 20-30 minutes. 3) Wait for the scheduled pin-healthcheck (runs every 30m). 4) Immediately after healthcheck completes, a subset (~7-12%) of requests switch egress via us-east edge then back within 20-90s. 5) During the flip p95 jumps to ~400-500ms for affected requests. Observed behavior: healthcheck completion appears to trigger routing path recompute that allows non-resident egress for pinned routes briefly. Expected behavior: pinned traffic should remain egressed from the pinned region unless a sustained failure is detected and routed by explicit fallback policy. Logs / traces: - Router trace sample (trace id: t-20260310-0a9c): shows route decision change at 2026-03-10T14:30:12Z. - Router debug: "pin_healthcheck: window=30s, result=OK, recompute_routes=true" - Edge connection logs show transient TLS renegotiation and elevated SYN/ACK RTTs to eu-west gateway during flip. Customer impact notes: affects production latencies for key API endpoints (inference and embeddings). Customer has asked for immediate mitigation and explanation.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: healthcheck completion triggers route recompute which evaluates fallback rules and may allow non-resident egress briefly. Evidence: correlated timestamps between healthcheck job and router decision changes; increased TCP retransmits to eu-west at the same time. Reproduction: internal load test with pinned workspace reproduced flip within healthcheck window. Root cause candidate: recompute logic does not enforce pin-strong preference during transient gateway degradation; a single OK/ degraded signal from healthcheck is treated as sufficient to allow fallback. Additional signal sources (edge TCP metrics) influenced decision path. Impact scope: appears limited to dedicated workspaces with pin and healthcheck enabled; not widespread across hosted customers. Temporary mitigation successful: disabled recompute-triggered fallback per workspace. Longer-term: require N consecutive failed/healthy checks and add a cooldown before allowing cross-region fallback for pinned routes. Added metric: 'egress_flip_count' with tags workspace and region.
resolution: Workaround applied: configured notifyly-prod to ignore healthcheck-triggered fallback for next 72 hours; this stabilized p95. Engineering fix planned: patch router to require 3 consecutive healthcheck results and a 60s cooldown before allowing fallback for pinned routes. PR redwood/router#4123 created; queued for canary deploy in US staging on 2026-03-15 and full rollout week of 2026-03-22. Post-deployment actions: - Add Console alert for 'egress_flip_count' > 5/min per workspace. - Update regional egress runbook to include steps for pin-healthcheck anomalies. - Notify affected customers and provide audit of temporary config changes. Linked follow-ups: infra/egress-gw#198 to review gateway retransmit behavior. Ticket will be updated when PR is merged and deployed.
